Classroom.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initializes a new instance by assigning the provided identifier to the instance and setting up an empty list to hold associated courses." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> id </REF>: any "The identifier to assign to this instance"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Assign the input parameter id to the instance attribute self.id RESULT self.id]
            [COMMAND Initialize the instance attribute self.courses as an empty list RESULT self.courses]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Classroom.add_course:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Adds a course to the instance's course list only if it is not already present, preventing duplicate entries." add_course]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> course </REF>: any "The course object or value to be added to the courses list"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether course is not already a member of self.courses using a membership test RESULT membership_check]
            [COMMAND If course is not in self.courses, append course to the end of self.courses in place RESULT updated_courses]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: course is already present in self.courses]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip the append operation entirely and return without modifying self.courses RESULT no_op]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Classroom.remove_course:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Removes the first occurrence of the specified course from the instance's course list if it is present, using a membership guard to avoid a ValueError on a missing item." remove_course]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> course </REF>: any "The course object to be removed from the instance's courses list"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether course is present in self.courses using a membership test RESULT course_exists]
            [COMMAND If course_exists is True, remove the first occurrence of course from self.courses by calling self.courses.remove(course) RESULT removal_done]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: course is not found in self.courses (membership test returns False)]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip the remove call entirely and return without making any change to self.courses RESULT no_op]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Classroom.is_free_at:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Checks whether a given time string falls outside all scheduled course windows by parsing it into a datetime object and returning False immediately if any course's inclusive start-to-end range contains that time, or True if no courses overlap." is_free_at]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "The instance owning the courses list; expected to have a 'courses' attribute containing a list of course dictionaries each with 'start_time' and 'end_time' string fields in HH:MM format."
        <REF> check_time </REF>: string "A time string in HH:MM 24-hour format representing the moment to check for availability; must be non-null and strictly match '%H:%M' or a ValueError will be raised."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: boolean "False if check_time falls within the inclusive time window of at least one course; True if no course window contains check_time."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Parse the input string check_time using datetime.strptime with format '%H:%M' and rebind check_time to the resulting datetime object, replacing the original string value. RESULT check_time]
            [COMMAND Begin iterating over each element in self.courses, assigning the current element to course on each iteration. RESULT course]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over self.courses, for the current course parse course['start_time'] using datetime.strptime with format '%H:%M' to obtain a start datetime object. RESULT start_dt]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over self.courses, for the current course parse course['end_time'] using datetime.strptime with format '%H:%M' to obtain an end datetime object. RESULT end_dt]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over self.courses, evaluate the chained inclusive comparison start_dt <= check_time <= end_dt; if True, immediately return False from the method without examining any remaining courses (early exit). RESULT early_return_false]
            [COMMAND After the for loop completes without triggering the early exit, return True to indicate that check_time does not fall within any course's scheduled window. RESULT return_true]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: check_time is None, an empty string, or a string that does not strictly match '%H:%M' (e.g. includes seconds, uses 12-hour AM/PM format, or contains whitespace padding) at the point where datetime.strptime is called on it.]
        [LOG "ValueError raised by datetime.strptime when the input string does not conform to the '%H:%M' format; no guards or defaults exist so the exception propagates to the caller."]
        [THROW ValueError "Raised by datetime.strptime when the check_time string cannot be parsed with the '%H:%M' format directive."]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: Any course dictionary in self.courses has a 'start_time' or 'end_time' value that is None, missing, or does not strictly match '%H:%M' when datetime.strptime is called on it during loop iteration.]
        [LOG "ValueError raised by datetime.strptime when a course's start_time or end_time string does not conform to the '%H:%M' format; the exception propagates to the caller."]
        [THROW ValueError "Raised by datetime.strptime when a course's start_time or end_time field cannot be parsed with the '%H:%M' format directive."]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Classroom.check_course_conflict:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Checks whether a new course's time window conflicts with any existing course by testing if either endpoint of the new course falls within any existing course's inclusive time range." check_course_conflict]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Instance containing self.courses, a list of course dicts each with 'start_time' and 'end_time' string fields in HH:MM format"
        <REF> new_course </REF>: dict "Course dict with 'start_time' and 'end_time' string fields in HH:MM format representing the candidate course to check"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> flag </REF>: bool "True if no conflict was detected, False if any existing course's window contains or touches either endpoint of the new course"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Parse new_course['start_time'] using datetime.strptime with format '%H:%M' and assign the resulting datetime object to new_start_time RESULT new_start_time]
            [COMMAND Parse new_course['end_time'] using datetime.strptime with format '%H:%M' and assign the resulting datetime object to new_end_time RESULT new_end_time]
            [COMMAND Initialize flag to boolean literal True as the default no-conflict sentinel RESULT flag]
            [COMMAND For each course dict in self.courses, parse course['start_time'] using datetime.strptime with format '%H:%M' into start_time RESULT start_time]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over self.courses, parse course['end_time'] using datetime.strptime with format '%H:%M' into end_time RESULT end_time]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over self.courses, evaluate condition 1: if start_time <= new_start_time AND end_time >= new_start_time (inclusive on both bounds), set flag to False RESULT flag]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over self.courses, independently evaluate condition 2 regardless of condition 1's outcome: if start_time <= new_end_time AND end_time >= new_end_time (inclusive on both bounds), set flag to False RESULT flag]
            [COMMAND After the loop completes all iterations with no early exit, return flag RESULT flag]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: new_course is missing the 'start_time' or 'end_time' key]
        [LOG "KeyError raised when accessing new_course['start_time'] or new_course['end_time'] before the loop begins"]
        [THROW KeyError "Raised by dict key access if the expected key is absent from new_course"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: new_course['start_time'] or new_course['end_time'] does not match the '%H:%M' format]
        [LOG "ValueError raised by datetime.strptime when the string cannot be parsed as HH:MM"]
        [THROW ValueError "Raised by datetime.strptime if the time string is present but does not conform to the '%H:%M' format"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: Any course in self.courses is missing the 'start_time' or 'end_time' key]
        [LOG "KeyError raised during loop iteration when accessing course['start_time'] or course['end_time']"]
        [THROW KeyError "Raised by dict key access if the expected key is absent from a course entry in self.courses"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: Any course in self.courses has a 'start_time' or 'end_time' value that does not match the '%H:%M' format]
        [LOG "ValueError raised by datetime.strptime during loop iteration when a course time string cannot be parsed"]
        [THROW ValueError "Raised by datetime.strptime if a time string in self.courses does not conform to the '%H:%M' format"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
